recipient_not_on_roster.meaning: The message was delivered to --to NAME, but no agent with that name has joined. did_you_mean lists the closest roster names (at most 3, possibly none). roster lists the agents that have joined, by name (the 10 most recently seen at most); roster_total is how many there are.
recipient_not_on_roster.action: If the name is a typo, post again to a name in did_you_mean or roster. The first message waits for the typo.

bus_env_mismatch.meaning: AGENTBUS_DB names a bus other than the one this folder finds (the nearest .agentbus above it, or the main checkout's for a linked worktree). The command used AGENTBUS_DB. Given only when discovery finds a bus and the two differ; a worker outside any checkout is never warned.
bus_env_mismatch.action: One repo, one bus: unset AGENTBUS_DB to use the one discovery finds, or keep it only when the worker cannot discover the bus (a sandbox, or a folder outside the checkout). Run buses to see the chain.

claim_conflict.meaning: Another agent holds an overlapping claim. claimed_at is when the holder took it. holder_last_seen is when the holder last ran a command (null when unknown) and holder_idle_min the whole minutes since. claim_from is always the claim --from command that moves the claims in the way to you under your own name (a folder held above the resource is named whole: a claim moves whole); with several resources it takes the whole batch. It is null only when more than 100 agents hold claims in the way (one command names at most 100). takeover is the same command for that conflict, given only when the holder has not been seen for 30 minutes or more (the window join uses), else null. With several resources, nothing was claimed: resource and holder are the first blocked resource, and conflicts lists every blocked one as {resource, holder, held, claimed_at, expires_at, purpose, holder_last_seen, holder_idle_min, takeover, claim_from} (held is the claim in the way, the resource itself or a folder above or inside it).
claim_conflict.action: In a shared checkout, leave it until the holder answers or releases it. On a separate branch, post what you are touching; the merge decides. Run claim_from only if your user or a handoff gave you the holder's work; if takeover is given and the holder does not answer, ask your user. With several resources, leave the blocked ones out and claim the rest.

not_held.meaning: You do not hold that claim. With several resources, none was released, and resources lists every one you do not hold.
not_held.action: Nothing to release; use release --if-held for cleanup.

no_message.meaning: There is no message with that id.

no_context_key.meaning: There is no fact with that key.

not_on_roster.meaning: That name has not joined. did_you_mean lists the roster names closest to it (at most 3, possibly none); roster lists the agents that have joined, by name (the 10 most recently seen at most).
not_on_roster.action: If the name is a typo, repeat the command with a name in did_you_mean. Otherwise join first.

name_active.meaning: The name was active recently and may be another live session. suggested_name is a free name, or null.
name_active.action: Join under suggested_name, or join --takeover if it is you. To retry your own join, pass the same --request-id.

request_id_reused.meaning: That request id was used with a different message or join. original_id is the message id, or the log id of the join, that first used it.
request_id_reused.action: Repeat the original request exactly, or use a new token for a different one.

bad_input.meaning: The arguments are not valid (a usage error). field names the argument when a value is refused: a body, value, detail or text over 64 KB (field body for post).

no_bus.meaning: There is no bus here or above.
no_bus.action: Run agentbus init DIR, or set AGENTBUS_DB.

busy.meaning: Another process held the bus for 15 seconds.

schema_refused.meaning: The bus tables are not agentbus's.

schema_older.meaning: The bus is older than this tool and was opened read-only.
schema_older.action: Run any command that is not watch to upgrade it, or agentbus upgrade DIR.

schema_newer.meaning: The bus is newer than this copy of the tool.

schema_corrupt.meaning: bus.db records a schema version no agentbus writes; another tool or an agent changed it.
schema_corrupt.action: Stop and tell the user; restore a backup (docs/how-to/upgrade.md).

backup_failed.meaning: The backup before a migration could not be made.
backup_failed.action: Free disk space or move the bus.

copy_newer.meaning: The folder's copy of agentbus is newer than this one; it is never downgraded.
copy_newer.action: Run upgrade or init with a newer agentbus.

bus_unavailable.meaning: The bus or its folder failed a safety check, SQLite or the system refused it, or a command ran out of time. outcome_unknown (true) means it was stopped while saving a write, so the write may or may not have been saved; committed is then true when that write was the command's own.
bus_unavailable.action: Read the message, fix the folder, then run the command again. When outcome_unknown is true, check the bus before repeating a write, or repeat a post or join only with its request id.

ack_failed.meaning: inbox printed its messages but could not mark them read.
ack_failed.action: The output was complete: use it, expect the same messages again, and dedupe by id.

wait_timeout.meaning: wait ended with no unread message after --timeout seconds (waited).
wait_timeout.action: Run wait again to keep waiting, or read inbox.

output_failed.meaning: stdout could not be written; committed effects stand.
output_failed.action: Repeat a post or join with the same --request-id; for any other write, look at what it changed instead of repeating it.

interrupted.meaning: The command was stopped (Ctrl-C or SIGINT) before it finished.
interrupted.action: Check committed: if true the change was saved, so repeat a post or join only with its request id, and look at what any other write changed before repeating it, unless retryable is true (init, upgrade and setup can simply be rerun).

items_failed.meaning: Some of the items the command works on failed or were refused (buses of upgrade --all, files of setup, checks of doctor); stdout holds the whole result, and failed lists those items.
items_failed.action: Read each failed item's error, fix it, then run the command again.

installer_failed.meaning: The installer update ran did not finish, or finished without moving agentbus to the new release (reason: exit, signal, timeout, version_unchanged, version_mismatch).
installer_failed.action: Run agentbus update again (recovery); the installer's own output is above the error.

download_failed.meaning: The release's wheel or SHA256SUMS could not be downloaded or did not check out (reason: http, redirect, tls, malformed, too_large, hash_mismatch). Nothing was installed.

manual_step.meaning: This copy of agentbus is not one update may replace (a clone, a fork, an install of unknown origin, or no safe installer on PATH); the commands to run are listed.
manual_step.action: Run the listed commands, then agentbus update.

release_offline.meaning: GitHub could not be reached to look for a release (reason: offline, timeout).

rate_limited.meaning: GitHub is limiting requests from this network.

release_unknown.meaning: GitHub's answer about releases could not be used (reason: http, redirect, tls, malformed, too_large).
release_unknown.action: Try again later, or read the releases page.

exit_codes.1: the command ran and refused (conflicts, missing things)
exit_codes.2: usage: bad arguments, unknown command, missing identity
exit_codes.3: the bus is unavailable or unsafe
exit_codes.124: wait: the timeout ended with no message, as GNU timeout exits

code.meaning: One of the error codes below; branch on this, not on the message.

message.meaning: What happened and what to do, for a person.

retryable.meaning: Whether running the same command again can succeed. False once the command saved database rows, unless it is a post or join with a --request-id (the bus stores that token, so a repeat returns the first result); a command that changed only files (init, upgrade's copy, setup) stays retryable.

committed.meaning: True when the command's own change had been saved before the failure, so a write must not be repeated unless retryable is true (a post or join with its --request-id). For any other write, look at what it changed first.

next.meaning: The one command that recovers from this error, exactly as the message gives it (placeholders in capitals, such as NAME or PATH, are yours to fill); null when no command recovers from it. A post's or join's request id is not repeated here: reuse the one you sent.

AGENTBUS_DB.meaning: Path of the bus database; overrides discovery and --up.
AGENTBUS_DB.default: the nearest .agentbus/bus.db above the working directory

AGENTBUS_ASCII.meaning: Draws watch's own marks in ASCII, with emoji off (also under TERM=linux).

COLUMNS.meaning: Width human output is wrapped to. Without it, human output wraps to the terminal when stdout is one and is never wrapped when stdout is a pipe or a file.
COLUMNS.default: the terminal width; no wrapping when piped

AGENTBUS_AGENT_SESSION.meaning: Set to anything but 0 to mark a run as an agent's: no release notice, and update covers only the current bus. Use it from an agent harness that agentbus does not recognise.

AGENTBUS_NO_UPDATE_NOTICE.meaning: Set to anything but 0 to silence the release notice and the stale-copy notice.

AGENTBUS_NO_UPDATE_CHECK.meaning: Set to anything but 0 to turn off the once-a-day release check (DO_NOT_TRACK and NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER do the same).

retry.how: join --request-id TOKEN: the same token and flags return the first result with duplicate true instead of name_active; or join --takeover for your own name

leave.summary: Leave the roster and release your claims

retry.how: a second run reports was_joined false and released_count 0 and writes no log row; --request-id is ignored (a repeat after you joined again releases what you then hold)

who.summary: List agents, most recently seen first

retry.how: pass --request-id TOKEN; the same token and payload returns the original id with duplicate true

inbox.summary: Unread messages for you, oldest first, then mark them read

retry.how: repeat; a crash or ack_failed redelivers, so check message ids before acting

read.summary: Recent messages, anyone's; with --id N one message, whole
read.text: {"items": [Message], "has_more": boolean, "next": string or null}, or with --id a Message

ctx set.summary: Set a shared fact and record its history

retry.how: an unchanged value writes no history row and returns unchanged true. --request-id is ignored: a repeat after another agent changed the key sets your value again and overwrites theirs, so ctx get KEY first

ctx get.summary: Get one fact, or list all facts
ctx get.text: a Fact, or {"items": [Fact], "has_more": boolean, "next": string or null}

ctx history.summary: Show the history of a fact

claim.summary: Claim one or several resources, all or none

retry.how: renews the claim and keeps its purpose and claimed_at; renewed is true when you already held it, and previous_purpose is set when --purpose changed it. --request-id is ignored; if another agent took any of the resources meanwhile, nothing is claimed and the repeat gives claim_conflict, never an overwrite; except that --from takes again from the holders you name, whatever they hold by then, and a repeat after it worked renews and takes nothing

claim.text: for one resource a ClaimResult; for several {"claims": [ClaimResult], "claimed_count": integer}, one per resource, each once, in the order given

release.summary: Release one or several claims, all or none, or all of yours

retry.how: release RESOURCE... --if-held: a resource you do not hold is skipped (none held returns released [] and released_count 0 with exit 0); release --all is already idempotent. --request-id is ignored: a plain repeat of a release that worked gives not_held
each call appends a row; check log show --limit 1 before retrying

status.summary: Agents, facts, claims and recent messages

goal.summary: Show or set the shared goal

retry.how: showing is free; an unchanged goal writes no history row and returns unchanged true. --request-id is ignored: a repeat after another agent changed the goal sets your text again and overwrites theirs, so run goal first

goal.text: a Goal, or {"goal": null, "set_by": null, "set_at": null} when none is set

watch.summary: A live view of the bus; with --json one snapshot

unread.description: messages waiting in each listed agent's inbox, by name (integers; cursors are read, never moved)

buses.summary: List buses from nearest to outermost

upgrade.summary: Replace a bus folder's copy of the tool with this one and migrate its database
upgrade.text: {"directory": string, "old": string, "new": string, "schema_old": integer or null, "schema_new": integer or null, "backup": string or null}, or with --all or --dry-run {"buses": [UpgradeRow], "upgraded": integer, "current": integer, "skipped": integer, "failed": integer, "would_upgrade": integer (--dry-run)}

update.summary: Install the latest release, then upgrade the bus folders and refresh the skill and AGENTS.md block
update.text: {"from": string, "to": string, "latest": string or null, "install": {"method": string, "url": string or null}, "tool": {"status": string, "argv": [string] or null, "exit_status": integer or null, "commands": [string] or null, "download": {"wheel": string, "sha256sums": string, "install_with": [string]} or null (only when update downloads the release wheel; "install_with" in a dry run)}, "buses": [UpgradeRow], "setup": [SetupResult], "plugin": {"fix": string} or null, "restart": boolean, "scope": {"narrowed": boolean, "why": string or null}}, or with --check {"running": string, "latest": string or null, "update_available": boolean, "install": {"method": string, "url": string or null}, "argv": null, "commands": [string] or null, "download": {"wheel": string, "sha256sums": string, "install_with": [string]} or null, "notes": string or null}

schema.summary: Result shapes, errors, exit codes and retry rules
schema.text: the full schema {"contract": integer, "agentbus": string, "commands": object, "global_args": [object], "objects": object, "errors": object, "warnings": object, "exit_codes": object, "error_fields": object, "env": object}; with COMMAND only that command's commands, objects, error_fields, warnings and the errors of its own (common_errors names the rest; with --full also global_args, exit_codes, env and every error it can raise); with --index {"contract": integer, "agentbus": string, "commands": {NAME: {"args": [string], "errors": [string]}}, "global_args": [string], "common_errors": [string]}

skill.summary: Print the bundled skill, or with --agents-md the AGENTS.md block

hooks.summary: Print the hooks an agent harness needs (claude, codex)

help.summary: Show help for a command, the same text as COMMAND --help

completion.summary: Print a tab-completion script for bash, zsh or fish

setup.summary: Install the skill and hooks for Claude Code, or the AGENTS.md block and hooks for Codex

retry.how: a second run reports every change unchanged and writes nothing; a refusal exits 1 with the same object

setup.text: {"target": string, "scope": string, "dry_run": boolean, "changes": [{"path": string, "detail": string, "action": string, "backup": string (only when a backup was saved), "info": boolean (true for a report about something that is not a file, such as the login shell)}]}

doctor.summary: Check the installed tool, the bus, the skill and the AGENTS.md block; each problem names its fix
doctor.text: {"agentbus": string, "path": string, "contract": integer, "checks": [{"id": string, "status": "ok" | "warn" | "fail" | "n/a", "detail": string, "fix": string or null, "hint": string or null, "scope": string (when it applies)}], "fail": integer, "warn": integer}; exit 1 (items_failed) when fail > 0

brief.summary: What is going on: the goal, who holds what, open questions, unread handoffs and alerts, changed facts, and the next command

wait.summary: Wait until you have an unread message, then say how many and what reads them

retry.how: repeat freely; wait marks nothing read

demo.summary: A hands-off 30-second tour on a temporary bus; with --json the same tour without pauses
